commits.summary: Harden trace redaction and add a pre-publish scan
commits.body:
Redaction policy 4 follows an external review of the published traces, which found the Anthropic organization UUID, the hostname and a third-party email in the logs of the first session. It adds the hostname, Windows account names, account identifiers inside strings, every email that is not public by design, wrangler's OAuth tokens, the Langfuse Basic auth header, and many more credential formats: URL and curl passwords, KEY=VALUE secrets, JWTs, and GitLab, Google, Stripe and other keys.

New guards: sync.py scan previews a publish and masks its output; upload_log refuses a log the current rules would still change; push runs check before uploading as well as after; check now also covers committed summaries and manifests, and audits published logs, reporting findings as notes. unpublish --reason withdraws a log, deletes the local copy and records why, and the summary lists it.

These changes were written by another agent whose session is not in this project's transcripts, so the session traced here is the one that reviewed the diff and committed it, not the one that wrote it. Verified by compiling sync.py, running 12 made-up inputs through the redactor (each redacted or kept as intended, idempotent, no leaks), and running check and scan before the commit: 0 errors. Logs already on the CDN are not changed by this commit.
Brings the published traces up to this point: conversation that came after a session's last commit, and sessions with no commit of their own.

commits.summary: Record that findings in published logs are accepted
commits.body: The stricter redaction rules flag 13 policy 3 logs from the first session that are already on the CDN. They were reviewed and judged innocuous, and the maintainer decided not to withdraw them, so CLAUDE.md and the history note in the specification now tell future agents to treat those check notes as warnings that need no action. Logs not yet uploaded are still held to the rules. Docs only; verified with sync.py check.
